subject: Console: ownership model for per-route cost & latency slices — decision and exceptions
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: jasmine.liu@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, aditya.rao@redwood.com
Cc: irene.choi@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Console: ownership model for per-route cost & latency slices — initial ask

Team —

Quick context: several recent tickets (see HubSpot/ACME-4521) and a QBR ask from Acme (below) surfaced inconsistencies in how we present per-route cost/latency slices in the Console. Product needs a small, defensible decision so we can: 1) show a clear owner in the UI, 2) ensure sampling/trace retention defaults are sane, and 3) document an exceptions workflow for multi-team tenants.

Top asks:
- Proposal: add a single "Primary Owner" field to the route meta + optional cost-center tags. Owner should be a single team inbox (email) rather than a person to avoid churn.
- Default sampling: 1% for high-volume public routes, 10% for tenant slices > $500/month — need engineering feasibility and cost estimate.
- Exceptions: define an on-call + product approval path for SLA/billing disputes; tie to an internal runbook.

Attachments: slice-ownership-runbook-draft.md (draft) + sample-rate-matrix.csv

Can eng confirm feasibility and a rough implementation timeline? Product to propose exact UX copy.

Thanks,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: slice-ownership-runbook-draft.md (text)]

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: hannah.schmitt@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 11:03:15 -0700
Subject: Re: Console: ownership model for per-route cost & latency slices — initial ask

Thanks Hannah — good to see this surfaced. Short thoughts from Product: 

- Owner as a team email: +1. Also add an owner-type enum (Product / Platform / Customer Success) so rollups can aggregate cost by organization.
- Sampling defaults: we should make these configurable per-tenant in the Console with clear minimums; otherwise ops will keep requesting one-off exceptions.
- UX: show owner, cost center, and a one-click "Request exception" that opens a pre-filled Doc with the current metrics (cost last 30d, p99 latency). That reduces back-and-forth with Finance/CS.

I've added a short mockup in the doc: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1a2b3c-slice-ownership-draft (see section "Request exception").

Jasmine
Product Manager — Observability

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Cc: aditya.rao@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Console: ownership model for per-route cost & latency slices — feasibility notes

Hannah / Jasmine —

Engineering feasibility notes: we can add a primary-owner meta field + cost-center tags in the route index within 2 sprints, but a few constraints:
- Telemetry tagging: we need a migration to populate owner tags for existing routes (we can backfill from repo + Git blame but expect ~10% ambiguity).
- Sampling controls: adding a per-route sampling toggle is straightforward; exposing per-tenant retention/sampling in the Console requires storage changes (estimating +10% infra cost until TTL rules are in place).
- Cost breakdown: we can show token-level cost and host (GPU/CPU) split, but per-tenant GPU attribution will be approximate initially until we complete the KV-cache-aware accounting work.

Actionable asks for Product: please prioritize whether the Console should show
  a) host-level breakdown (GPU vs CPU) or
  b) model-level breakdown (model family, quantization) as default.
We can ship (a) faster; (b) is useful but needs kernel-selection tagging in traces.

I'll draft a minimal inspector tile prototype this sprint.

Ben
Engineering Manager, Observability
[Attachment: sample-rate-matrix.csv (csv)]

From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acmecloud.com>
To: hannah.schmitt@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 23 Aug 2026 10:10:00 -0700
Subject: Acme QBR request: per-route cost + latency report

Hannah / Marissa —

Following up on our QBR prep: can you provide a per-route cost & p95/p99 latency spreadsheet for our top 25 routes for the last 90 days? Finance (cc'd) needs a clear mapping of which Redwood team owns each route for chargeback.

Deadline: Wed, 26 Aug EOD (we know this is short notice). If a full export is hard, a breakdown with owner + 30/60/90d cost is sufficient.

Thanks,
Priya Shah
Head of Platform — Acme Cloud
[Attachment: acme-cost-request.pdf (pdf)]

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: priya.shah@acmecloud.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, jasmine.liu@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Cc: aditya.rao@redwood.com, irene.choi@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 24 Aug 2026 14:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme QBR request: per-route cost + latency report / internal decision

Priya —

We can deliver a scoped export for the top 25 routes by Wednesday EOD. Internal decision items (so Acme and Finance know the constraints):

1) Ownership model: we're adopting the "Primary Owner (team inbox) + Owner Type" model. Default owner for legacy routes will be Platform until product owners confirm. We'll surface owner in the Console and include it in the export.

2) Sampling & retention: export will use current sampling logic. Product has an action to make sampling configurable in-console (see Jasmine's doc). Full per-tenant retention controls will be tracked in the roadmap — expect a Q4 ETA for retention knobs.

3) Cost attribution caveat: GPU vs CPU split is available, but per-tenant GPU attribution is approximate today; we'll call that out in the export and include a short note.

Action items assigned:
- Ben: ship the inspector tile prototype and the export endpoint for top-N routes by Wed EOD (ACME-4521).
- Marissa: prepare the export template and cover note for Finance.
- Jasmine: add the exception request UX copy to the doc.
- Aditya/Irene: coordinate the migration plan for owner backfill.

Deliverables: export (CSV) + cover note + one-pager caveats.

Hannah
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference
